result.process_description:
First, the implements are prepared, the hands are washed, and the doctor gets in sterile clothes.
The doctor cleans the puncture area, and drapes the puncture zone.
The doctor configures the ultrasound, and puts gel in the probe.
Then, the doctor covers the probe and puts the sterile gel.
The doctor positions the probe and positions the patient.
The vein is identified using an anatomic identification, a doppler identification, or a compression identification.
The patient is anesthetize and punctured.
The blood return is checked.
If the blood return is not correct, the doctor goes back to the puncture step.
If the blood return is correct, the probe is dropped and the syringe is removed.
The guidewire is installed, and the trocar is removed.
Then the wire is checked using a check of the wire in the long axis, or a check of the wire in the short axis.
Then, the doctor checks if the wire is in good position.
If the wire is not in the good position, the doctor goes back to the puncture step.
If the wire is in the good position, the pathway is widen, the catheter is advanced, and the guirewire is removed.
Finally, the doctor verifies the flow and the reflow, and the catheter position is checked.

result.rule: Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.

result.rule: When the description says that an activity may recur and that each occurrence requires a subsequent activity to happen again.: Model the recurring behavior with a gateway-controlled path that ensures each occurrence is followed by the required subsequent activity, rather than using only a one-time direct sequence.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before the process continues: Model mutually exclusive paths for performing or skipping the activity, then merge the paths before the next step.

When the description identifies alternative outcomes or case types that require different follow-up paths, with one path possibly returning to earlier work: Model an exclusive gateway with a separate flow to each applicable follow-up path, including a return flow when a path resumes earlier work.

When the description places a decision or synchronization point after an activity: Connect the preceding activity to that gateway with a sequence flow in the same process scope; do not omit the transition.
